title: A governed deletion withholds its whole generation; re-creation is a fresh, isolated generation; deleted versions are as-of barriers

invariants.statement: After a governed deletion no version of the deleted generation is admitted to current or historical recall, nor by logical reference, and the owner's history reads tombstoned with no events, live and after restart.
invariants.falsified_by: any deleted version admitted or any event served

invariants.statement: The owner's re-creation is visible only as its own generation: old versions are withheld from recall, history (its whole payload) and write_semantics.
invariants.falsified_by: an old version, its identifier or its text surfacing

invariants.statement: Another project's re-creation is isolated both ways: the former owner reads nothing of it and cannot write, correct, delete or dispute it (answering exactly as it would with no re-creation, except that a remember on an open id is the documented disclosure); the new generation reads nothing of the former.
invariants.falsified_by: any cross-generation read, an admitted former-owner write, or a former-owner answer that differs from the control

invariants.statement: Every deleted version is an as-of barrier for every reader, and a live generation resolves only for its owner, only from its own start.
invariants.falsified_by: version_in_effect resolving a deleted version, or resolving the live generation for a non-owner

invariants.statement: A governed deletion of one superseded version withholds only that version, live and after restart; a deleted head or lineage member cannot be deleted again (already_deleted) and the attempt leaves the recorded tombstone (deleted_at, version, lineage) unchanged, live and after restart.
invariants.falsified_by: the deleted version admitted, a sibling version withheld, a re-deletion committed, a changed tombstone record, or a former version resurfacing after restart

invariants.statement: After a permanent deletion the canonical substrate holds no fact of the lineage, no public read of any scope serves an identifier or text of it, the derived-store reconciliation reports complete, and the owner still reads tombstoned. This is a claim about canonical facts and public reads only, not about rollback journals, WAL frames, backups, snapshots or the filesystem (docs/28: no full-deletion claim where it cannot be demonstrated).
invariants.falsified_by: a surviving canonical fact, an identifier or text in any public read, an incomplete reconciliation, or a non-tombstoned owner view

Versions are generation-relative ... After a governed deletion of the head the id reports `0` to any writer, a re-creation's receipt reads `v0 -> v1`, and the former generation's count never reaches the new one; the owner of the deleted generation still reads the version its deletion recorded (`tombstoned`, DUR-DEL-001).

`remember` onto a live head outside the writer's scope: `committed: false`, `refusal: "target_unavailable"`, receipt `before_state`/`after_state` `v0`, `state_snapshot` `v0`. Nothing is written, no episode is retained, no version moves.
A refused `promotion` tells the writer that the id is unavailable to it.

A governed-deleted generation is closed. At the fact level (`dispute` of a tombstoned fact by its uuid, a governed pruning of one of its versions, the adapter's delete of a member of a deleted lineage) the answer is `already_deleted`; at the facade's logical-reference level (`forget`, permanent `forget`, `correct`, `dispute` by `target_reference`) the former owner reads the bare `fact_not_found` result ... Either answer is the same whether or not another scope has since re-created the id, and neither moves or reads the live generation
